claimed.text: George Knapp testified under oath in September 2025 that Robert Bigelow and an AAWSAP colleague negotiated with senior Lockheed Martin executives for a quantity of unusual material held at a facility in California, and named Lockheed as one of the corporations holding it.

Luis Elizondo told the House in November 2024 that the Lockheed Martin transfer to Bigelow's company was blocked, and that a required Secretary of the Air Force memorandum never issued; he also agreed that material is routed to contractors by expertise, aerospace to Lockheed.

UAP Gerb said on NewsNation in August 2026 that KONA BLUE was a DHS-brokered programme through which Lockheed Martin material was diverted before the CIA shut it down; AARO's own account records the proponents' belief that existing holdings could be moved under KONA BLUE for congressional oversight.

Ben Rich is alleged to have said in a 1993 talk that the means to travel among the stars already exist inside black programmes; the board holds this at Tier 3, since attendees recount variants but no recording, transcript or letter exists.
Mark McCandlish relays an unnamed informant who said he worked at the B-2 facility at Plant 42, and who places the Skunk Works near the plant; the account is relayed, unnamed and uncorroborated.

Tom DeLonge wrote to Podesta that when Roswell crashed it was shipped to the laboratory at Wright-Patterson, which General McCasland had run until a couple of years before, and that the general had helped assemble his advisory team.

The board infers that the unnamed facility in California of Knapp's testimony is most plausibly a Lockheed site in the Palmdale area, because Knapp named California and Lockheed; no witness has named a site.

contested.text: AARO's report states that it found no empirical evidence that the government and private companies have been reverse-engineering extraterrestrial technology, and that executives and technology chiefs of the companies named by interviewees denied such programmes on the record; it names no company and describes no inspection of any facility.
Nothing ties the Skunk Works to recovered material in the documents: the board's custodian argument rests on capability and precedent, and the one Rich remark in circulation has no primary record.

The Podesta release contains the DeLonge, McCasland and Lockheed correspondence, but not the Prometheus framing later attributed to it; a podcast guest who described that content said he was repeating what he had heard from someone else.
AARO offers KONA BLUE as a rejected proposal that witnesses mistook for an operating programme, and says the material it was to protect was only assumed to exist.

The GAO figures are often misquoted: the unresolved total was 11 documents, not 17 or 46, which were dispositions within the 224 later accounted for, and GAO itself had not verified Lockheed's reported results.

lead.text: Lockheed's Skunk Works is the documented builder of aircraft whose existence was officially denied while they flew, from the U-2 to the F-117, and Lockheed Martin is named in custody allegations, including sworn testimony. George Knapp testified that Lockheed held unusual material at a California facility; AARO says the executives of the companies named to it denied such programmes, and no record the board holds shows Lockheed holding recovered material.

record.text: Ben Rich directed Lockheed's Advanced Development Projects from 1975 to 1991 and published a memoir describing how its unacknowledged programmes were compartmented, staffed and funded at Burbank and Palmdale; the organisation operates at Air Force Plant 42 in Palmdale.
The CIA's history records Kelly Johnson on the April 1955 flight with Richard Bissell that found the Groom Lake site, and says Johnson named the base Paradise Ranch.

GAO's testimony of 24 July 1986 reports that Lockheed's inventory of about 40,000 secret and top secret items across 53 document control stations found 1,460 discrepancies; Lockheed reported, in results GAO had not yet verified, that 11 documents remained unresolved, 7 said to have been inadvertently destroyed and 4 not located.

GAO explained that in 1965 DoD excluded special access programmes from supervision by the Defense Investigative Service, so that special access contracts, which GAO estimated in 1983 to number several thousand, were carved out of its inspections, and concluded that it was inconsistent to create a special access programme for security and then give it less document protection than ordinary classified work.

The companion GAO letter of 7 August 1986 names the Lockheed Burbank plant, which the testimony withheld under an agreement with DoD, and says the failure might not have occurred had the Defense Investigative Service inspected that contract as it inspected Lockheed's other contracts.
AARO's Volume I names Lockheed Martin's Advanced Development Programs, with the RQ-170 and DarkStar, among classified aircraft mistaken for UAP.

The WikiLeaks Podesta emails show a Lockheed Skunk Works address copied on the January 2016 thread arranging a meeting between John Podesta, Tom DeLonge and General Neil McCasland, and DeLonge writing in February 2016 that Mr. Weiss from Lockheed SkunkWorks had asked him for updates.
Lockheed Martin is the largest single recipient of DoD prime contract obligations, in the hundreds of billions of dollars since FY2008.

summary.text: The documented half: Lockheed's Advanced Development Projects designed and flew the U-2, A-12 and SR-71 and F-117 under security regimes that denied them, and the CIA's own accounts say U-2 and OXCART flights were the source of a majority of UFO reports in the late 1950s and 1960s, with false explanations issued to protect them.

The oversight record: a 1986 GAO review of a Lockheed special access contract at Burbank found deteriorated document control, which GAO said might not have happened had the Defense Investigative Service been allowed to inspect the contract; special access programmes had been excluded from its supervision since 1965.

The alleged half: sworn testimony that Lockheed negotiated to transfer stored material to Robert Bigelow's company, that the transfer was blocked, and later claims that Lockheed-held material was to move under the proposed KONA BLUE programme.

The board's own reading is that an organisation able to fly unacknowledged hardware for years is a natural custodian for material the government would deny, an inference from capability and precedent, not a document.

title: Lockheed and the Skunk Works in the custody record
